T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — EPS growth >25% in H2 2026, AI infrastructure spending trajectory

Synopsis:
HSBC raised its S&P 500 year-end target to 8,100 (from 7,650), implying ~4.9% upside, driven by strong corporate earnings (86% Q2 beat rate vs. 67.5% long-term average) and sustained AI infrastructure spending. HSBC projects >25% EPS growth in H2 2026. Risks flagged include potential Fed rate hikes, geopolitical uncertainty, midterm elections, and AI/IPO-related liquidity demands — but HSBC views these as largely overblown. Tech valuation expansion is seen as constrained despite strong fundamentals. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup also target S&P 500 at or above 8,000.
